chunk-001:c001.proposition: An all-loving God who desires relationship with every person would not permit non-resistant nonbelief or the stark geographical distribution of faith.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Treating every conscious experience as divine presence does not establish the distinctively theistic claim that ultimate reality is a personal divine agent.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Even if cultural history nonculpably weakens awareness of God, perfect love should provide clear revelation once a person becomes responsible for belief.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: Gratuitous-seeming horrors give evil evidential force, while skeptical theism replies that finite humans cannot expect to comprehend an omniscient creator's reasons.

chunk-002:c002-02.proposition: Reliance on divine inscrutability to answer evil and hiddenness can undermine arguments that depend on understanding divine goodness and purposive fine-tuning.

chunk-002:c002-04.proposition: A personal divine commander may motivate morality better than an impersonal good, but grounding motivation in divine power risks reducing morality to coercion.

chunk-002:c002-08.proposition: Moral anti-realism can make moral judgment inherently motivating by incorporating emotion, avoiding the realist possibility of recognizing goodness without caring about it.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-03.proposition: Using Christianity's historical moral influence apologetically requires prior criteria for distinguishing genuine doctrinal development from corruption.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: A realist account of moral development must explain delayed discovery without retrofitting progress or surrendering the timelessness of moral truth.
